summary: If /usr/bin/python is missing or incompatible on a remote host, set ansible_python_interpreter to the right Python path; the same pattern works for other languages (ansible_ruby_interpreter, ansible_perl_interpreter), and module shebangs should not be edited.
questions: My host only has python3 and not /usr/bin/python, how do I tell Ansible?
How do I point Ansible at a custom Python on a managed node?
Can I set the interpreter for Ruby or Perl modules?
Should I change the shebang in my custom modules?

answer_card.title: Set the remote Python interpreter
answer_card.answer_md:
Set **`ansible_python_interpreter`** in inventory or vars:

```ini
host1 ansible_python_interpreter=/usr/bin/python3
```

Ansible rewrites module shebangs at run time, so **don't edit shebangs** yourself. The same works for other languages: `ansible_ruby_interpreter`, `ansible_perl_interpreter`, etc.
